newsitem.title: FRANCE: Mitterrand aide Sautter new French budget minister.
newsitem.headline: Mitterrand aide Sautter new French budget minister.

text.p: Christian Sautter, a specialist in international economics, was named secretary of state for the budget in France's new government on Wednesday, inheriting the tough task of keeping public spending under control for a single European currency.

Sautter, 57, was long an aide to late president Francois Mitterrand, rising to deputy head of the president's private office, and is one of just a few economic policy makers with the ear of new Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's ear.
The budget portfolio is a junior ministry under Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn with responsibility for the day-to-day management of the budget.
During Jospin's 1995 run for the presidency, Sautter headed the Socialists' economic policy experts group, managed the party's economic proposals and grew close to its leader.
Described as courteous, discreet and secretive, he is a graduate of the elite engineering school Ecole Polytechnique and holds advanced degrees in economics and politics.
Sautter's career has traced lines typical for high civil servants in France, moving from elite educational institutions to senior governmental posts.
He was government prefect for the giant Paris region in the early 1990s, administering the most populous and richest of France's 22 regions.
Sautter is the author of several books on the Japanese economy including his latest, "France in the face of Japan: competition or decline", published in 1996.
